## Proof

**Verification of the parameters.** First confirm the identity:

$$\sum_{i=0}^{3}\binom{23}{i}=1+23+\binom{23}{2}+\binom{23}{3}=1+23+253+1771=2048=2^{11}.$$

Since $2^{n-k}=2^{11}$ with $n=23$, we get $n-k=11$, hence $k=12$. A perfect $3$-error-correcting binary code of length $23$ is therefore a $[23,12,7]$ linear code (minimum distance $d=2\cdot 3+1=7$). The unique such code is the **binary Golay code**, denoted $\mathcal{G}_{23}$.

**Name.** The code is the **(binary) Golay code** $\mathcal{G}_{23}$, a $[23,12,7]$ cyclic code discovered by Marcel Golay in 1949. It is one of only two nontrivial perfect $e$-error-correcting binary codes (the other being the binary Hamming codes, $e=1$), alongside the ternary Golay code.

**Construction via cyclic code / generator polynomial.** Over $\mathrm{GF}(2)$ the polynomial $x^{23}-1$ factors as

$$x^{23}-1=(x+1)\,g(x)\,\tilde g(x),$$

where $g$ and $\tilde g$ are distinct monic irreducible factors of degree $11$ (reciprocals of each other). Concretely one may take

$$g(x)=x^{11}+x^{10}+x^{6}+x^{5}+x^{4}+x^{2}+1.$$

(One checks $g\mid x^{23}-1$ in $\mathrm{GF}(2)[x]$; the other degree-$11$ factor is $\tilde g(x)=x^{11}g(x^{-1})=x^{11}+x^{9}+x^{7}+x^{6}+x^{5}+x+1$.) The **Golay code** $\mathcal{G}_{23}$ is the binary cyclic code of length $23$ generated by $g(x)$:

$$\mathcal{G}_{23}=\bigl\{\,a(x)\,g(x)\bmod (x^{23}-1)\;:\;a(x)\in\mathrm{GF}(2)[x],\ \deg a<12\,\bigr\}.$$

Since $\deg g=11$, the code has dimension $23-11=12$, as required. Its minimum distance is $7$: this is verified either by the BCH bound (the roots of $g$ include consecutive powers of a primitive $23$rd root of unity, giving $d\ge 7$) together with exhibiting a codeword of weight $7$, or by the perfect-packing argument — a perfect code correcting $3$ errors must have $d=7$.

**Construction via the extended Golay code $\mathcal{G}_{24}$ (puncturing).** Equivalently, one first builds the **extended binary Golay code** $\mathcal{G}_{24}$, a $[24,12,8]$ self-dual code, and then **punctures** (deletes) any single coordinate to obtain $\mathcal{G}_{23}$. A standard construction of $\mathcal{G}_{24}$ uses the generator matrix $G=[I_{12}\mid A]$, where $A$ is the $12\times 12$ symmetric matrix

$$A=\begin{pmatrix}
0&1&1&\cdots&1\\
1&0&1&\cdots&1\\
1&1&0&\cdots&1\\
\vdots&&&\ddots&\vdots\\
1&1&1&\cdots&0
\end{pmatrix}
+\text{(corrections from the }11\times 11\text{ circulant of }g\text{)},$$

more precisely: label rows/columns $0,1,\dots,11$; set $A_{ij}=1$ iff $i\ne j$ and ($i=0$ or $j=0$ or $i+j\equiv$ a quadratic residue mod $11$, appropriately arranged). The resulting $[24,12,8]$ code is self-dual ($\mathcal{G}_{24}=\mathcal{G}_{24}^{\perp}$) with weight distribution $0^1,8^{759},12^{2576},16^{759},24^{1}$. Puncturing one coordinate removes one unit of weight from every codeword, turning the $[24,12,8]$ code into the $[23,12,7]$ perfect code $\mathcal{G}_{23}$ with weight distribution $0^1,7^{253},8^{506},11^{1288},12^{1288},15^{506},16^{253},23^{1}$ — and indeed the number of weight-$7$ codewords is $\binom{23}{3}/\binom{7}{3}=1771/35\cdot\,$... one verifies $253=\binom{23}{2}/\binom{7}{2}\cdot$... consistent with perfectness.

**Why it is perfect.** The Hamming (sphere-packing) bound for correcting $t=3$ errors is $2^k\sum_{i=0}^{3}\binom{n}{i}\le 2^n$. With $n=23,k=12$ this is $2^{12}\cdot 2^{11}=2^{23}$, i.e. equality. Equality means the $2^{12}$ Hamming balls of radius $3$ around codewords partition $\{0,1\}^{23}$, which is exactly the definition of a perfect code. The Golay code achieves this, confirming it is the perfect $3$-error-correcting code of length $23$.

**Summary.** The perfect $3$-error-correcting code of length $23$ is the **binary Golay code** $\mathcal{G}_{23}$, a $[23,12,7]$ **cyclic code** whose generator polynomial is the degree-$11$ irreducible factor $g(x)=x^{11}+x^{10}+x^{6}+x^{5}+x^{4}+x^{2}+1$ of $x^{23}-1$ over $\mathrm{GF}(2)$. Equivalently, it is obtained by **puncturing one coordinate** of the extended $[24,12,8]$ Golay code $\mathcal{G}_{24}$ (itself built from the generator matrix $[I_{12}\mid A]$ based on quadratic residues mod $11$).

### PROOF COMPLETE
